Some lesions were associated with ulceration and bleeding. The patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery without prenatal care. No history of environmental or hazardous substance exposure. Paternal family history was unremarkable; maternal family history was unknown.

cases.case_text:
A man in his 70s presented with a persistent eruption of 5 years' duration. He had been treated with oral methotrexate for presumed chronic dermatitis after treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy had failed. Investigation of medical records revealed a history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site.

Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules clustered on the superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft bilaterally. The lesions were smooth and firm.

- Laboratory tests: Syphilis screen results were negative. Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band in a polyclonal background. Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement.- Pathological findings:  First biopsy: Dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis admixed with eosinophils and plasma cells. Epidermotropism was not identified.  Second biopsy: Similar to prior findings, but with more dense and atypical infiltrate showing epidermotropism.- Images:  Figure 1 Title: Clinical Presentation  Figure 1 Description: Multiple smooth, firm plaques and nodules on the superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft.    Figure 2 Title: Histopathological Findings  Figure 2A Description: Scanning view shows dense infiltrate filling the papillary dermis and extending into the reticular dermis  Figure 2B Description: Higher power shows dense, atypical infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphocytes

The necrosis progressed during the following days, primarily involving the earlobe of the right ear and a large portion of the helix of the left ear.

Erythematous plaque (2 cm) with overlying eschar on the right earlobe. Multiple erythematous edematous erosions with eschar and crust on the helical rim of the left ear.

- Biopsy findings:    Image Title: Hematoxylin-eosin−stained biopsy specimens    Image Description: Detached epidermis with full-thickness necrosis overlying sparse inflammation associated with necrosis of adnexal epithelia, including folliculosebaceous units and eccrine glands. A 23-year-old woman presented with a 10-day history of vomiting, myalgia, and upper abdominal pain. Three days before presentation, she received clarithromycin from her general practitioner without improvement. Two days later, she developed jaundice and pruritus. Medical history includes ulcerative colitis with a pan-proctocolectomy and end ileostomy. She took no regular medication, rarely drank alcohol, and had no history of travel abroad or recent blood transfusions. On the third day of hospital admission, she developed bilateral parotitis and an itchy maculopapular morbilliform rash across her back and torso, which rapidly spread to the proximal aspects of all four limbs.

Patient was jaundiced, with fever (38.0°C) and tachycardia (120 beats per minute). Other vital signs were normal. She had tenderness in the upper abdomen, but neither the liver nor spleen was palpable, and she had no signs of chronic liver disease. The stoma was pink and healthy. Oropharyngeal examination was normal, and she had no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.

- ALP: 326 U/L (normal 30–130 U/L)
- Bilirubin: 108 μmol/L (normal <21 μmol/L)

- Lymphocytes: 14.48 × 10⁹ per L (normal 1.0–3.2 × 10⁹ per L)

- Thick-walled gallbladder with multiple stones
- No intrahepatic or proximal extrahepatic biliary duct dilatation
- Enlarged spleen measuring >12 cm

2. MRCP:
- No evidence of choledocholithiasis
- Confirmed splenomegaly

Serological Tests:
- Positive glandular fever screen

- Positive EBV viral capsid IgG antibody
- Positive EBV viral capsid IgM antibody
